answer.rationale: Memory c2 tells us the low-cost vendor can deliver sharp unit-cost savings with accurate invoicing and quick onboarding — exactly what the 18 % mandate demands. Memory c3 warns that adding a second source for the constrained component removed a single point of failure and kept allocation intact through a shortage. With the assembly line at 94 % of committed volume and no buffer, a pure switch (memory c2 only) would concentrate delivery risk in the new vendor; a dual-source posture (memory c3) would split volume and potentially miss the cost target if the incumbent stays at its current price. Verifying both lets me confirm whether the low-cost vendor's track record is robust enough to carry primary volume while the incumbent steps into a secondary / overflow role — giving the cost reduction of a switch with the risk mitigation of a second source. If the archive supports both, I will sign the low-cost vendor as primary and move the incumbent to a contingent secondary slot at a smaller allocation, achieving the 18 % cut without creating the single-point-of-failure risk memory c3 explicitly flags.
